title: Find the rule engine at startup, not on the first order

blocks.text: The shop keeps its discount rules as small scripts, such as `total > 480`, so that the marketing team can change them without a release. The rules used to run on the JDK's own JavaScript engine. After the move to a new Java release, the service started cleanly and then failed on the first order that had a discount, with a `NullPointerException`.

The team has added a script engine as a dependency, and the configuration now lists the engine names to try, in order of preference. Finish `pickEngine(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/DiscountRules.java` so that rules run on the first configured engine that is installed, and so that a service with none of them installed fails while it starts, with `DiscountRules.NoScriptEngine` and a message that names the engines it looked for. About five lines.
The tests register their own small engines under names such as `graal.js` and `rhino`.

cases.says: with the configured engine installed, rules are evaluated by it and give the right answer
when two configured engines are installed, the one named first is used
when no configured engine is installed, building the rules fails with NoScriptEngine naming every engine it looked for
when the first configured engines are not installed, a later one that is installed is used

origin.section: Nashorn Is Gone, and the Engine Lookup Returns null Instead of Failing

concepts: With Nashorn removed in 15, ScriptEngineManager.getEngineByName returns null for a missing engine, so the failure appears where the engine is first used unless startup checks it.
